answer: Memory-hard per-action puzzle resists sybils: each action must solve a scrypt-style puzzle whose cost is dominated by large RAM held for the whole computation, bound to the identity key and a fresh challenge. Memory bandwidth, not raw compute, is the floor, so parallel hardware barely helps. A river of fakes each pays the full memory cost per action, so aggregate RAM-seconds wander upward linearly with head count, never reaching a cost nadir from sharing, since each key's challenge forces a distinct allocation. Precondition: puzzle memory exceeds cheap reuse and challenges are key-bound.
